sentences.text:
1 learned Senior Advocate for Respondent No.1 in Criminal Application No.377 of 2022 and Ms. 1 of 10 Appln.501.22 & Appln.377.22.doc Phad, learned APP for Respondent No.2 - State.
2.

This is a group of two Interim Applications filed by Applicant - Original Complainant - Sunil Giri seeking cancellation of the following impugned orders passed by the learned Sessions Court, Dindoshi, Mumbai in connection with FIR No.755 of 2022 registered on 21.07.2022 with Vile Parle Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 409, 465, 467, 468, 471 read with Section 120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'IPC').

(i) Order dated 08.08.2022, granting anticipatory bail to Respondent - Accused No.3 (Jairaj Bafna).
The said impugned order is appended at Exhibit 'C' - page 87 of Criminal Application No.501 of 2022.
(ii) Order dated 18.08.2022 granting regular bail to Respondent - Accused No.4 (Sunil Jain).
The said impugned order is appended at Exhibit 'C' - page 89 of Criminal Application No.377 of 2022.

2.1. These Applications are heard alongwith Anticipatory Bail Application Nos.2677 to 2022; 2754 of 2022; 2857 of 2022; 3537 of 2023; 2723 of 2022; 2669 of 2022; 2682 of 2022 and 2751 of 2022 wherein both private Respondents are Applicants.
I have passed orders today itself in the above ABAs and allowed the same.

To appreciate and adjudicate the present Applications,
it would be necessary to consider the brief facts relevant for adjudication which are in a very narrow compass.
Applicant is the same in both these Applications which arises out of the same cause of action.
Hence these Applications are disposed of by this common order.
2.3. Applicant was introduced to Accused Nos.3 and 4 by Mr. Umesh Malaye and was advised to invest in 'Future and Options' trading.
It is stated by Applicant that though he filled the account opening forms, he did not submit them.
While Applicant and his wife were abroad, Accused No.3 informed him that a Demat Account was opened in the name of his partnership firm - Blue Sea International.
Applicant stated that he did not submit the forms, to which Accused No.3 replied that process was initiated and it would require formal submission of documents.
Applicant agreed to this and subsequently transferred large sums to Artha Vriddhi Securities Ltd. (for short 'AVSL') as investments for trading.
It is admitted that both Accused persons from time to time sent to the Applicant his account's profit and loss statement.
2.4. However in June 2021, Applicant discovered that the Accused persons were not trading as instructed and had sent fabricated reports to him.

Hence he demanded a refund of Rs.1,47,09,150/-
after deducting loss of Rs.79,62,049/- from the balance amount of 3 of 10 Appln.501.22 &
Appln.377.22.doc Rs.2,26,71,200/- as reflecting in his account by a set-off.
However both Accused persons failed to return the amount, thereby he has alleged that they committed cheating.
On 17.07.2021, Applicant approached National Stock Exchange (for short 'NSE') and registered his Sunil Kundan Singh Giri vs Sunil Rikabchand Jain And Anr.

2 complaint.
Subsequently Applicant alleged that his account opening forms were uploaded with forged signatures while he was abroad.
2.5. Hence on 21.07.2022, Applicant lodged FIR No.755 of 2022 against four accused persons.
Accused No.3 applied for anticipatory bail which was granted on 08.08.2022.
Accused No.4, arrested on 24.07.2022 was also granted regular bail by order dated 18.08.2022.
2.6. Aggrieved by the said orders dated 08.08.2022 and 18.08.2022, Applicant has filed present Criminal Applications seeking cancellation of the bail orders.

3. Mr. Rajput, learned Advocate for the Applicant would submit that Accused No.3 in connivance with Accused No.4 defrauded Applicant and other investors by diverting funds to the accounts of Mr. Ritesh Jain and Mrs. Urvi Milan Shah.
He would submit that the fraudulent intent existed from inception.
He would submit that the learned Sessions Court failed to consider the charge of fabrication of documents, including the forged signature appended on the account opening form submitted to the bank.
3.1. He would submit that accused persons are habitual 4 of 10 Appln.501.22 & Appln.377.22.doc offenders.
He would submit that apart from the present FIR, there are two other FIRs pending against them for similar offences.
He would submit that there are a total of 22 complaints which have been lodged against AVSL on the NSE portal pointing out a widespread and recurring pattern of market abuse and public deception.

3.2. He would submit that the Sessions Court failed to consider that Accused Nos.3 and 4 in collusion with each other forged documents, manipulated trades without consent of the investors and issued over 300 fake emails misrepresenting shareholding positions.

3.3. He would submit that by order dated 18.02.2022 NSE observed that AVSL filed certificates reflecting net worth in excess of Rs.1 crore, however it failed to deduct non-allowable assets such as doubtful debts and advances which resulted in the actual net worth standing at a negative Rs.1.67 crores and Rs.1.48 crores for the period of March 2021 to September 2021.
He would submit that this concealment establishes suppression of material facts and misrepresentation of finances thereby indicative of dishonest intent.

3.4. He would therefore submit that these statutory and regulatory violations recorded by the NSE after following the due process are admissible and relevant material that go to the root of the matter.
He would submit that Applicants cannot wash their hands off such misconduct while having played key roles in sales and client 5 of 10 Appln.501.22 & Appln.377.22.doc relations.

Hence, he would urge the Court to quash and set aside the impugned orders passed by the Sessions Court granting Anticipatory Bail and Regular Bail to Accused Nos.3 and 4.
4.

PER CONTRA, Mr. Mundargi, learned Advocate appearing for Respondent - Accused No.3 (Jairaj Bafna) in Criminal Application No.501 of 2022 would argue in support of the impugned order dated 08.08.2022 granting Anticipatory Bail.
He would submit that Accused No.3 is falsely implicated in the present crime.
He would submit that Applicant was a Business Consultant with AVSL on a retainer-ship basis.
He would submit that Applicant was not an employee and was not involved in its day-to-day affairs.
He would submit that his role was limited to customer relationship coordination and operational support.
He would submit that the Trading/Demat account of Blue Sea International was opened by Relationship Managers Mr. Nilesh More and Mr. Umesh Malaye after due verification.
He would submit that no specific role was attributed to Accused No.3 in the present crime.

He would submit that no money trail has been discovered linking Accused No.3 to the alleged Sunil Kundan Singh Giri vs Sunil Rikabchand Jain And Anr. on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82191035/
3 offense.

sentences.text: He would submit that chargesheet is filed and investigation is completed and no recovery is to be made at the instance of Accused No.3.
Hence he would urge the Court to dismiss Criminal Application No.501 of 2022.

5. Mr. Parab, learned Senior Advocate appearing for 6 of 10 Appln.501.22 & Appln.377.22.doc Respondent - Accused No.4 in Criminal Application No.377 of 2022 would argue in support of the impugned order dated 18.08.2022 granting Regular Bail.

He would submit that Applicant has been falsely implicated and made a scapegoat in the present FIR, which selectively states names of Accused Nos.3 and 4 despite the fact that funds were transferred to AVSL's corporate accounts and not to the personal accounts of the accused.
He would submit that day-to-day affairs of AVSL including financial decisions were handled by Dhirendra Shukla and his family members who were authorised signatories.

He would submit that Applicant has not been issued any notice or faced action from NSE, BSE or SEBI till date and all transactions were routed through recognised exchanges with due credit to clients' accounts and no illegality is attributed to Accused No.4.
He would submit that there is no financial trail linking Accused No.4 to any alleged offence.
He would submit that three FIRs on the same cause of action have led to parallel investigations in FIR No.755 of 2022.
In the present crime, investigation is completed, relevant documents and bank statements have been disclosed and provided.
Hence he would submit that present Application is an abuse of the due process of law and therefore deserves to be dismissed.

6. Ms. Phad, learned APP for Respondent No.2 - State would adopt the submissions made by Mr.
Rajput.

She would submit that both Accused persons were actively involved in the commission of 7 of 10 Appln.501.22 & Appln.377.22.doc offences which involved unauthorised trading,
misappropriation of funds and fabrication of documents.
She would submit that the claim that funds were routed through AVSL's official accounts does not absolve Applicants of their individual roles in the illegal scheme.

There are serious allegations of wrongful gains transferred to related parties including co-accused's relatives which require custodial interrogation to unearth the financial trail and digital evidence.

Hence she would urge the Court to quash and set aside the impugned orders passed by the learned Sessions Court granting Anticipatory Bail and Regular Bail to Accused Nos.3 and 4.
7.
I have heard the learned Advocates appearing for the parties and learned APP for the State and with their able assistance perused the record of the case.
8. At the outset, it is seen that allegations in the FIR pertain to financial misappropriation and forgery in the context of securities trading.
It is pertinent to note that cause of action arises out of long standing commercial transactions between Applicant and AVSL wherein Applicant invested money for trading in F & O through AVSL.
It is not disputed that the funds were transferred to the corporate accounts of AVSL.

9. With regard to Accused No.3 - Respondent in Criminal Application No.501 of 2022, anticipatory bail was granted by the 8 of 10 Appln.501.22 & Appln.377.22.doc Sessions Court after considering the material on record and noting that there was no direct money trail linking Accused No.3 to the alleged misappropriation.

The Sessions Court also noted that the role attributed to Accused No.3 Sunil Kundan Singh Giri vs Sunil Rikabchand Jain And Anr. on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82191035/
4 was not supported by sufficient prima facie evidence warranting custodial interrogation.

entities.text: Accused No.3 Sunil Kundan Singh Giri vs Sunil Rikabchand Jain And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is seen that the charge- sheet has been filed and investigation is complete.

It is settled position of law that bail once granted can be cancelled only in cases where there is violation of bail conditions,
tampering of evidence, or threat to witnesses, none of which is demonstrated in the present case.

10. With regard to Accused No.4 - Respondent in Criminal Application No.377 of 2022, the Sessions Court has rightly exercised its discretion in granting regular bail after taking necessary facts into consideration and the fact that investigation is completed and no further recovery is to be made.
It is seen that prosecution has failed to placed any credible material showing a direct financial link between Accused No.4 and the alleged fraudulent transactions.
Mere association with AVSL is insufficient to deny bail once investigation is concluded is what is held.

11. The argument of the Applicant that there exist multiple complaints against the Accused persons on the NSE portal and that they are habitual offenders cannot be the sole ground for cancellation of bail in the present matter.
9 of 10 Appln.501.22 & Appln.377.22.doc 12.
It is settled law that bail once is granted it should not be lightly cancelled unless there are supervening circumstances or material suppression of facts at the time of grant of bail.
No such circumstance is made out in the present case in respect of both Accused persons.

On Applicant's own showing it is borne out that he received the benefits of trading for a substantial period of time and it is only when his account was not settled by AVSL that he is aggrieved.
13.
In view of the above observations and findings, I am of the opinion that no case is made out for interference with the impugned orders passed by the learned Sessions Court, Dindoshi.
Hence in that view of the matter Criminal Application No.501 of 2022 and Criminal Application No.377 of 2022 stand dismissed.
The impugned orders dated 08.08.2022 and 18.08.2022, passed by the Sessions Court, Dindoshi are upheld and confirmed.
14. All contentions of the parties are left open to be adjudicated at the time of trial.
The observations made herein are only for the purpose of adjudication of the present Criminal Applications and shall not influence the trial in any manner.
15. Both Criminal Applications are dismissed and disposed.
[ MILIND N. JADHAV, J. ]
